successors.note: Pannonian Avars page: the Avars 'conquered and incorporated various nomadic tribes - Kutrigurs and Sabirs' and 'By 562 the Avars controlled the lower Danube basin and the steppes north of the Black Sea'; the avar-khaganate dossier founds the Avars on the Pontic steppe in 561 (Cliopatria's year). Kutrigur remnants were 'swept away by the Avars to Pannonia' (10,000 under Bayan in 568) and the name returns in Kubrat's Old Great Bulgaria, 630-635 (Kutrigurs page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 551-561: the Kutrigurs on the western Don-Azov steppe. 'Procopius says they occupied this zone [the Tanaitic-Maeotic, Don-Azov steppe], with the Kutrigurs in the western part'; in 551 Chinialon's army came 'from the western side of the Maeotic Lake' to aid the Gepids; in the winter of 558 Zabergan's army crossed the frozen Danube. The page gives no area or boundary, only the 'Pontic-Caspian steppe in the 6th century'; the shape (Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Kherson, about 80,000 km2) is a reading. The avar-khaganate shape of 561 (655,633 km2, the lower Danube basin and the Pontic steppe east to about 39E) covers this land from 561. Infobox area: none on the page.

ledger.note: 551: the first dated Kutrigur army. Chinialon's army came 'from the western side of the Maeotic Lake' to aid the Gepids (Kutrigurs page); Pseudo-Zacharias lists the 'kwrtrgr (Kutrigurs)' among 13 tribes about 555. The pages give no founding of a Kutrigur state and nothing between the Hunnic collapse (469, huns dossier) and 551: the year is the first date at which the people appear, a bridge.

region.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone, the Kutrigurs in the Western part': the steppe on the western side of the Sea of Azov and the lower Dnieper

ledger.note: About 561: the Avars take the Pontic steppe. The Avars 'conquered and incorporated various nomadic tribes - Kutrigurs and Sabirs - and defeated the Antes'; 'By 562 the Avars controlled the lower Danube basin and the steppes north of the Black Sea' (Pannonian Avars page). The pages do not date the conquest of the Kutrigurs; 561 is the year Cliopatria's Avar shape and the avar-khaganate dossier begin (the page says 'by 562'). Kutrigur horsemen still serve the Avars: 'Bayan I commanded an army of 10,000 Kutrigur Bulgars and sacked Dalmatia in 568'.

region.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone, the Kutrigurs in the Western part': the steppe on the western side of the Sea of Azov and the lower Dnieper

ledger.note: About 561: the Kutrigur realm is absorbed. 'Some Kutrigur remnants were swept away by the Avars to Pannonia' and the Kutrigurs were absorbed by the Avars toward the end of the 6th century (Kutrigurs page, which gives no year); the Zabergan page lists Zabergan as 'Leader of the Kutrigurs: fl. 558-586', succeeded by Bulgarios. Dissolution year follows the Avar page ('by 562') and the avar-khaganate dossier (561).

wars.name: Kutrigur invasion of the Balkans
wars.outcome: Zabergan crosses the frozen Danube in the winter of 558 and attacks Constantinople in March 559 with 7,000 horsemen; Belisarius defeats him at Melantias and he withdraws. 2,000 Kutrigur horsemen later entered imperial service and were settled in Thrace (Kutrigurs page, undated).
wars.note: A raid, not a conquest: no land changed hands. Other raiding groups reached Thermopylae and the Thracian Chersonesus (Kutrigurs page).

wars.name: Utigur-Kutrigur war

zones.text: 'the Don-Azov steppe zone, the Kutrigurs in the Western part': the steppe on the western side of the Sea of Azov and the lower Dnieper

wars.outcome: Justinian 'managed to persuade the Utigur chieftain Sandilch to attack the Kutrigurs, which resulted in the decimation of both' (Zabergan page); 'ultimately the two peoples decimated one another' (Kutrigurs page).
wars.note: No page dates the war; it is bracketed between Zabergan's retreat (559) and the Avar conquest (by 562).

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-f (counterparts_needing_dossiers 'Kutrigurs', years not given; 'eu-06-x or ia-01'). Three pages opened. This is a people known from Procopius and Menander, not a state with a documented territory: the dossier's years (551-561) are the first dated sighting and the Avar conquest, its region a reading of one phrase, and every event is confidence 1. The huns dossier (eu-06-a) ends the Huns in 469 and says the Kutrigurs and Utigurs are 'other peoples' and that the Pontic steppe passes to no state until Old Great Bulgaria (633); this dossier does not claim continuity with the Huns (the Kutrigurs page makes them 'remnants of the Huns' only in Grousset's view, and Golden links them to the Oghur tribes). The Kotzagiroi (possibly Kutrigurs) fled to the Avars from the Türks by 569 (Kutrigurs page). Overlap: the avar-khaganate 561 shape. Old Great Bulgaria (ia-01, 633-668) unites 'the Onogur Bulgars with the tribes of the Kutrigurs and Utigurs' between 630 and 635; the avar-khaganate dossier's 656 note quotes the Old Great Bulgaria page on Kotrag, 'the leader of the Kutrigurs'. Gazetteer: all names resolve. Wikidata id unknown.
